title: Mixing Routing Mechanisms with Specific Policy Rules
pattern: @Core search or traversal mechanism contains hardcoded, specific conditional statements defining specific selection or filtering policies.
why_bad: The algorithm (the mechanism of pathfinding/graph traversal) is coupled to volatile business rules (routing specifications, hazard policies). This prevents the search algorithm from being reused or optimized independently.
detection: A pathfinder, query, or solver method directly references domain-specific properties of the items being processed to filter or score candidates inside the search loop.
counterexample: Generic heuristics (like cost/distance multipliers) that are passed to a pathfinder are highly appropriate. Marked `Context-dependent`.
source: Eric Evans, *Domain-Driven Design* (2003), Chapter 12, "Strategy (A.K.A. Policy)", p. 325.
